paragraphs.title: Completion of the Tabernacle and the Leaders’ Gifts

easy.explanation: Moses anointed and sanctified the tabernacle, its vessels, and the altar.
easy.q: What did Moses do to the tabernacle and its vessels?

easy.explanation: They brought six covered wagons and twelve oxen.
easy.q: What did the princes of Israel bring?

easy.explanation: The sons of Kohath received none because they carried the sanctuary vessels on their shoulders.
easy.q: To whom were no wagons given?

answers: According to the number of princes
medium.explanation: The wagons and oxen were given to every man according to his service.
medium.q: Why were the wagons and oxen distributed among the Levites?

medium.explanation: The sons of Gershon received two wagons and four oxen.
medium.q: How many wagons and oxen did the sons of Gershon receive?

answers: According to the needs of his assigned work
medium.explanation: The phrase shows that the gifts were suited to the work each Levitical family performed.
medium.q: What does “according to his service” mean in this passage?

answers: Their service was not performed with wagons
challenge.explanation: Their service required them to bear the sanctuary vessels upon their shoulders.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the fact that the sons of Kohath carried the holy vessels on their shoulders?

answers: Distribution according to the needs of the work
Distribution according to the prince’s tribe
challenge.explanation: The gifts were distributed according to the service of each Levitical family.
challenge.q: What principle is shown by the distribution of the gifts to the Levites?

answers: After the Tabernacle was prepared, the princes supplied means for its service and transport
challenge.explanation: After the Tabernacle was sanctified, the gifts helped the Levites carry out its service.
challenge.q: What is the connection between sanctifying the Tabernacle and the princes’ gifts?

paragraphs.title: The Order of the Altar Dedication

answers: For the dedication of the altar
For a journey in the wilderness
easy.explanation: The princes brought offerings for the dedicating of the altar.
easy.q: For what purpose did the princes bring their offerings?

easy.explanation: The LORD appointed each prince to offer on his own day.
easy.q: How many princes offered each day?

easy.explanation: Nahshon the son of Amminadab offered on the first day.
easy.q: Who offered on the first day?

medium.explanation: One prince offered on each day for twelve days.
medium.q: How many days did the offering schedule cover?

answers: Setting apart and beginning it for sacred use
medium.explanation: The dedication set the altar apart for its worship service.
medium.q: What does “dedicating” mean in “dedicating of the altar”?

answers: The offerings were made in an orderly manner
medium.explanation: The LORD established an organized daily order for the offerings.
medium.q: What does one prince offering on his own day show?

answers: The offerings were private and unrelated to the tribes
challenge.explanation: Each prince is identified as the prince of one of the tribes of Israel.
challenge.q: Why can the princes’ offerings be viewed as representing all the tribes?

answers: The princes brought the offerings, and the LORD established when each would offer
The offerings were divided before the Tabernacle was built
challenge.explanation: The princes brought offerings, and the LORD assigned each prince a day.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between verses 10 and 11?

answers: He was the first to offer
challenge.explanation: Nahshon offered on the first day of the altar’s dedication.
challenge.q: What distinguishes Nahshon from the princes described after him?

paragraphs.title: The Components of the First Leader’s Offering

easy.explanation: The offering included a silver charger.
easy.q: What was the charger made of?

easy.explanation: The golden spoon was full of incense.
easy.q: What was in the golden spoon?

easy.explanation: One kid of the goats was offered for a sin offering.
easy.q: What animal was offered for a sin offering?

medium.explanation: The silver charger and bowl were full of fine flour mingled with oil for a meat offering.
medium.q: What was in the silver vessels?

answers: A young bullock, a ram, and a lamb
medium.explanation: The burnt offering consisted of one young bullock, one ram, and one lamb.
medium.q: Which animals were offered for a burnt offering?

answers: An offering of fine flour mixed with oil
A vessel used to carry the Tabernacle
An offering consisting only of cattle
medium.explanation: The KJV uses “meat offering” for fine flour mingled with oil.
medium.q: In this passage, what is a “meat offering”?

answers: The vessels were presented together with their contents
The vessels were used to carry animals
challenge.explanation: The charger and bowl were full of flour and oil when presented.
challenge.q: What does the statement that both silver vessels were full emphasize?

challenge.explanation: The offering included burnt offerings, a sin offering, and peace offerings.
challenge.q: Which kinds of offerings together form the complete offering described?

answers: The offering included vessels and contents as well as animals
The offering consisted only of metal vessels
The offering consisted only of animals
challenge.explanation: The passage describes metal vessels filled with offerings together with several kinds of animals.
challenge.q: What does the combination of silver vessels, a golden spoon, and animals show?

paragraphs.title: The Sequence of Offerings and Repeated Pattern

easy.explanation: Nethaneel, prince of Issachar, offered on the second day.
easy.q: Who offered on the second day?

easy.explanation: Eliab, prince of Zebulun, offered on the third day.
easy.q: Who offered on the third day?

easy.explanation: Ahiezer, prince of Dan, offered on the tenth day.
easy.q: Who offered on the tenth day?

answers: Two oxen, five rams, five he goats, and five lambs
A wagon was brought each day
Only incense was offered each day
medium.explanation: The same numbers and kinds of animals are repeatedly listed for the peace offerings.
medium.q: What detail is repeated in the descriptions of the princes’ peace offerings?

answers: Each day is associated with the prince of a different tribe
Every day is associated with the prince of Judah
medium.explanation: The passage names a different tribal prince for each day.
medium.q: What is the relationship between each day and the prince named?

medium.explanation: A he goat is a male goat.
medium.q: What are “he goats” in the KJV wording?

answers: The list of offerings is repeated in nearly the same form
The entire offering changes every day
Only the names of the princes are repeated
challenge.explanation: The same vessels, animals, and quantities are listed for the successive princes.
challenge.q: What makes the repeated pattern in the chapter easy to recognize?

answers: A different tribal prince appears on each successive day
All the tribes appear on one day
challenge.explanation: The chapter presents one tribal prince after another in a daily sequence.
challenge.q: What connection exists between the sequence of days and the tribes?

answers: The leaders followed a consistent pattern in presenting their gifts
Every leader brought a completely different offering
challenge.explanation: The repeated wording shows that the offerings followed the same established pattern.
challenge.q: What does the repeated wording suggest about the offerings?

paragraphs.title: Summary of the Dedication and the Divine Voice

easy.explanation: The summary lists twelve silver chargers.
easy.q: How many silver chargers were counted in the summary?

easy.explanation: The summary lists twelve golden spoons.
easy.q: How many golden spoons were counted?

answers: From above the mercy seat, between the two cherubims
easy.explanation: Moses heard the voice from above the mercy seat upon the ark, between the two cherubims.
easy.q: Where did Moses hear the voice?

medium.explanation: The summary counts twelve bullocks for the burnt offering.
medium.q: How many bullocks were offered for a burnt offering altogether?

medium.explanation: The peace offerings included twenty-four bullocks.
medium.q: How many bullocks were counted for the sacrifice of peace offerings?

medium.explanation: The mercy seat was upon the ark of the testimony.

answers: The totals represent the gifts of twelve princes
The vessels belonged only to the sons of Kohath
challenge.explanation: The summary counts twelve chargers, twelve bowls, and twelve golden spoons, corresponding to the twelve princes.
challenge.q: What is the connection between the twelve princes and the number of silver and golden vessels?

answers: After the dedication, Moses’ communication with the LORD is described
The offerings ended communication with the LORD
challenge.explanation: After summarizing the dedication, the passage describes Moses entering the Tabernacle and hearing the voice.
challenge.q: What does the move from the summary of offerings to Moses hearing the voice show?

answers: From above the wagon of Gershon
challenge.explanation: The voice came from above the mercy seat, from between the two cherubims.
challenge.q: From exactly where was the voice heard?

short_answers.question: Who was the first prince to offer at the altar’s dedication?
short_answers.explanation: Nahshon offered on the first day.

short_answers.question: Why did the sons of Kohath receive no wagons?
short_answers.answer: They carried the sanctuary vessels upon their shoulders.
short_answers.explanation: Their assigned service required them to bear the holy vessels on their shoulders.

short_answers.question: What did Moses hear between the two cherubims?
short_answers.answer: The voice of one speaking unto him.
short_answers.explanation: Moses heard the voice from above the mercy seat upon the ark of testimony.
